transcript: Over half a million cars are stolen every year using this method. But you can protect yourself with a super simple trick that costs literally a penny. Step one is easy. Just never leave your keys right by the front door. But then for step two to play it safe, you need some earplugs for your key fob. Now you can buy these key fob protective security pouches for like 10 bucks, but just make sure you test them because two of the ones we bought to try out didn't work at all. So instead you could just try a cookie tin. And to prove how well this actually works, as you can see, I can open I open the door like this, but if I put it in the tin first, the key fob can't hear the car whisper, and that means the car door doesn't open up. And that works because the wireless signals want to take the path of least resistance. And since metal is much more conductive than air, the signal hits the outside here and travels just through the metal before continuing on. It's a protective electronic bubble we call a Faraday cage. Now, if you don't have a cookie tin on hand, one penny's worth of aluminum foil is enough to make a pouch that will plug your key's ears as you can see here.
metadata_caption: Stop Your Car From Getting Stolen!
